text: Aside from the tech hub here at Fortune Town, there's a supermarket located at the ground floor and a department store at the 2nd floor. I did check out the clothing department and bought a few t-shirts at really good prices. Staff is friendly and reminded us of a promo for certain purchases. Good customer service, clean and spacious retail area. Dropped by here after checking out the IT sector. Entrance to Lotus is the best place to grab a ride or taxi as it is very well known.

3.8⭐️
Lotus is the grocery store inside the Fortune Town mall. This is right behind the MRT station, and around the corner from our place. So it is our go to place for groceries. I give 3.8⭐️ because they do run out of things quickly. If you go right when they open it’s not an issue, but if you go later in the day, or try and do an online order for delivery, then they will probably be out of a lot. If you order online, beverages are normally the only things they are not out of 🤣 but I have had them say they were out of water twice when I ordered online. I asked for substitutions but they just removed them from my order. So it is easier to get what you need in person and earlier in the day.

Perfect place to buy your basic household needs. Fruits and veggies are fresh! They have plenty of promotion all the time. Excellent customer service. You can also ask them to cook a sumptuous meal for you at a very good price. The place is very clean and well maintained. The cashiers were fast and efficient. Prices are very competitive.

About Electronic store on the 2nd floor. Yes they sell many electronic item with cheap price, but be careful about the quality. We bought a water cooking machine just 2 week ago and now is not working. When come to Lotus they said they waranty only 7 days. If any question need to contact directly to the manufacturor. Their customer service is very bad, even we go with small baby sleep on troller they asked to go many place for asking, and then finally not help or waranty at all!

I purchased Häagen-Dazs vanilla ice cream from this shop because it was on sale. However, it tasted very bad. It lacked its usual smooth and rich flavor and was different from the one at Tops supermarket. I suspect it melted and was refrozen. Ice cream should not be refrozen and eaten!

The choices are good but about the fruits it’s quite disappointing, I expected more from a supermarket, the variety of options about the desserts (fruits especially) is really limited. And it’s quite disappointing the fact that the plastic is used for some ridiculous quantity of bananas, just a bag that is composed of plenty of bananas, that would be more interesting! The prices are good enough.

FOREIGNERS BEWARE: if you plan to use the self checkout they will watch you like a hawk even if there’s 5 other Thai people in the self checkout they will only watch you. I usually use the self checkout to avoid the long lines and the woman working at the self checkout stood uncomfortably close to me so I would notice her and look up at her and then she tries to pretend you need help but she’s really just trying to make sure you’re not stealing anything. The reason I know is because I told her I already know how to use the self checkout and instead of leaving you alone they stand there and stare. And then the security guard also came to watch me although there’s many Thai in the self checkout area, but they don’t watch any of them. I asked the security guard why they don’t watch the other Thai people and she just laughed and kept watching me. There’s literally other Thai people buying hundreds of baht worth of items but they only want to watch me, the only foreign person. No offense but I literally have more money in my bank than all of these employees put together and you want to treat me like I’m some sort of thief? Westerners aren’t stupid enough to come to a foreign country and risk getting their visa revoked by stealing from such an inexpensive supermarket that would cost them 3 times as much in their home country. I find their racial profiling and discrimination very rude and unnecessary. This establishment owes me an apology and those staff members need some retraining. FOREIGNERS, EXPATS, and WESTERNERS BEWARE!

The Lotus group in Thailand was once a branch of Tesco UK so visitors from the UK will understand that Lotus is a one stop shop.
This Lotus store is located at the end of Fortune Town, which is a few metres from
Phram 9 MRT station. Take the Fortune Town exit.
The store has a food hall where a multitude of freshly cooked Thai dishes is available at street market prices.
The lower level has fresh meat, fruit and vegetables for sale, along with every conceivable grocery item.
Also a fair selection of wines, spirits and beers.
Note: Alcohol sales are not permitted between 2pm and 5pm.
The upper level has a pharmacy, clothing , appliances and bedding.
Also on the upper level is a branch of DIY, a hardware store that sells: hand and power tools, screws and fasteners, electrical accessories, plastic products, kitchen and bathroom accessories etc, etc. all at very reasonable prices.

Big supermarked, but so many things missing in the total range.
On date of end if April they just done a big upgrade of the fresh food department. They cook what you buy now if you wish. Some tables (not many enough) to eat the prepared products. Looks great!
Also the rayons with frozen products get their renewing and upgrade. Looks much cleaner and modern in this stage.
Food court with affordable price, Thai tea for only 24baht

There is food court inside the mall, cost per plate around 55  to 60 Bth
Foods are delicious and place to seat down with AC.

I recently had the pleasure of visiting Lotus’s shopping mall in Bangkok, and I couldn’t be more impressed! The mall is so spacious, clean, and well-organized that it felt a breeze to wander around. There’s an amazing variety of stores, offering everything from luxurious brands to adorable local finds.

One of my favorite parts was the food court—it's a foodie paradise! You’ll find delicious Thai dishes alongside tasty international options, all at great prices. Plus, the staff are super friendly and ready to help, which made my visit even better.

Getting there is easy, too, with convenient parking and good access to public transport. Whether you’re hunting for trendy fashion, cool electronics, or even just some groceries, Lotus’s has something for everyone. I definitely recommend checking this place out if you’re in Bangkok—it’s a must-visit!
Loved the food stalls and the ambience. Most of all, there are so many camera shops. Competitive prices as well as genuine products. Many top brands such as Canon, Nikon are here

I am a Vietnamese tourist coming to Thailand for the first time. People here often advise me to go to Big C, but I went there, but I didn’t buy enough, so I came to try Lotus. Although the items here are not as diverse as Big C, they have all the things we need for tourists and they are not crowded, so they are very convenient. Maybe I’ll come back here next time.

There have been a few times that the vegetables looked old while on display, but I ignored that because I needed the food. Well now I bought chicken breast yesterday and it spoiled within 24 hours. The chicken they put out was already old. I'm not returning to this grocery store again.
Nice department store to shop for household requirements like fresh fruits & vegetables, spices, oil etc in the Rama 9 Area.
Great supermarket, fair price
Excellent spotless clean friendly staff good prices good parking  would be my preferred shop

I recently went shopping at Lotus Supermarket and want to share an important warning—please be cautious of thieves. During my visit, I used a trolley to collect items and placed my bag on it, which unfortunately contained $200 and my passport. It was stolen inside the store. I felt extremely disappointed and frustrated, especially since the staff were slow to respond and I found out that some areas of the supermarket don’t have CCTV coverage. My advice: always keep your bag with you and stay alert while shopping.

text: This branch is the worst for online orders. I've considered stopping ordering from them, but this time I accidentally ordered from this branch. The product delivered smelled bad, was almost rotten, and was of poor quality.

For those arriving by motorcycle, I recommend parking in front of Lotus (the Rider parcel pick-up point). If you ask the security guard where to park, they might suggest parking on the 4th floor, which is on the opposite side of Lotus, and then you'll have to walk and take the elevator down to the 1st floor.

Parking for less than 10 minutes costs 10 baht because there's no free parking for the first hour. The parking system is confusing for motorbike and bicycle users; the management isn't very efficient.
